item.title: Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop (18 minute read)
item.description: Folding routers, planners, and domain specialists into a single agent loop can reduce lossy handoffs, cost, and latency when skills and tool search load context on demand. Anthropic describes migration patterns and evaluations for deciding which boundaries to remove. Separate agents still help with independent parallel work, verification, permission boundaries, and measurable context overload.

item.title: Anthropic builds its own source control system (12 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic replaced Git in its monorepo with Scion as daily merges grew from about 2,500 to more than 30,000 and CI reached 25 million checkouts a day. Its Rust client and server store changesets in Spanner and blobs in Google Cloud Storage, with a separate review system replacing GitHub's workflow.

item.title: We Built an AI Agent to Investigate Production Issues (10 minute read)
item.description: Stream's incident agent gathers logs, metrics, database results, and code references, then has a fresh session challenge its conclusions before posting findings. Read-only tools, isolated credentials, restricted networking, and output filters enforce its limits outside the prompt. Engineers approve every fix, while 22 evaluation cases test real incidents and past mistakes.

item.title: Docker is weird (3 minute read)
item.description: Building a container runtime exposes Docker as a collection of Linux mechanisms, including namespaces, cgroups, and filesystem isolation around ordinary processes. This walkthrough explains why Go's multithreaded runtime complicates container setup and why rootless networking often requires extra work in userspace.

item.title: Speeding up code review with small-change (5 minute read)
item.description: Imprint is testing a faster review path for narrowly scoped changes as rising PR volume pushes median review time from 33 to 77 minutes. Eligibility depends on a CI-controlled check covering change size, service experience, scope, and automated review findings, with shared libraries and sensitive paths excluded. Errors are treated as failures to improve in the verification system.

item.title: Is Your Organization Messing Up AI Adoption? (11 minute read)
item.description: AI adoption needs changes to incentives, working practices, and support alongside software licenses. Staff need role-specific training, time to experiment, and a reason to share in productivity gains without fearing punishment for mistakes. Shadow AI can reveal gaps in official tools that blanket restrictions only push out of sight.

item.description: TanStack AI brings 76 packages to stable APIs for chat, tools, media, MCP, persistence, and sandboxes while preserving provider and framework choice. Upgrade all client and server packages together and replace APIs deprecated in 0.x. The newly introduced agent harness remains experimental.

item.title: NVIDIA OpenShell (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenShell runs agents in policy-controlled sandboxes with kernel-enforced file and network limits, credential injection, and formal checks on proposed access changes.

item.title: Jailbreaking the Switch 2 (10 minute read)
item.description: ns2jb is a software-only, tethered jailbreak demonstrated on Switch 2 firmware 23.0.1. It enables native code execution for homebrew and game modifications.

item.title: How we cut GitLab Duo Code Review's cost by 98% (11 minute read)
item.description: AI21 combined a switch to DeepSeek V4 Flash with context compaction to cut GitLab Duo Code Review's estimated token cost from $0.589 to $0.0135 per pull request on a public benchmark, with F1 rising from 46.4% to 47.2%. Compaction made oversized reviews fit the deployment's context window, removing expensive fallbacks to Sonnet.

item.title: What the heck is the Public Suffix List? (21 minute read)
item.description: The Public Suffix List records the boundaries browsers and password managers need to distinguish independently controlled sites on shared domains. Its rules prevent cookies and saved credentials from crossing tenant boundaries, but growing demand leaves volunteers reviewing increasingly complex submissions. The article explains why DNS has not replaced the list and why using it for unrelated controls can create problems.

item.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale (15 minute read)
item.description: Claude produced machine-checked proofs for 239 fuzz-test entry points across 123 open-source libraries, turning existing tests into specifications over compiled RISC-V code. The guarantees cover inputs below 64 MB under a single-threaded Linux model with fixed memory limits, so they establish specific security properties rather than complete program correctness.

item.description: Making a screen's relevant state explicit lets people and agents inspect combinations of roles, plans, billing states, and feature flags before merging a change.

item.title: How ChatGPT's Ad Stack Works (12 minute read)
item.description: ChatGPT's ad system uses a post-trained LLM to orchestrate retrieval, ranking, relevance checks, and auctions as user intent evolves across conversations. Stateful ad sessions preserve context, while separate models, services, and code keep ad selection outside ChatGPT's answer-generation path.

item.title: Computing Bounding Boxes (6 minute read)
item.description: tldraw transforms shape vertices into page coordinates, then takes their minimum and maximum values to compute fast axis-aligned bounding boxes. The walkthrough covers nested transforms and rotated selection handles, with approximate bounds filtering candidates before more expensive geometry checks.

item.title: Front-end Observability at Scale with ClickHouse (11 minute read)
item.description: OpenReplay's largest customers ingest billions of events and roughly 6 TB daily on a single ClickHouse instance, with sub-second queries. Moving behavioral analytics out of Postgres also replaced disruptive retention cleanups with TTL rules and simplified data pipelines through materialized views.

item.title: The Web Is More Than Enough (6 minute read)
item.description: Modern browsers already offer cryptography, native-speed code, graphics, and audio, while AI makes those capabilities easier for individuals to use. Falling development and hosting costs could expand personal software creation and challenge app-store economics.

item.title: Asking LLM for Confidence (8 minute read)
item.description: An LLM's stated confidence is generated text, so a precise-looking number should not be treated as a calibrated measure of correctness. The proposed alternative derives scores from observable evidence and historical outcomes, then checks calibration regularly on the same kinds of tasks.

item.title: Who Holds the Off Switch? (24 minute read)
item.description: Five imagined coffee purchases in 2035 illustrate different models of data control, from state surveillance and privacy regulation to commercial data markets, public infrastructure, and biometric identity. Privacy increasingly depends on who can stop collection. AI assistants and paid privacy tiers will make that question more pressing.

item.title: Claude Duet (Website)
item.description: Claude Duet is a proactive agent that delivers morning briefs, handles tasks while you are away, and asks for approval when needed. The research preview uses Opus 5.5, carries over Claude memory, skills, and apps, and is offered through a waitlist for US Pro and Max users.

item.title: Omnara (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Omnara is an open-source managed agent platform that can run with different model providers and execute tools on sandboxes or your own machines. A REST API, TypeScript SDK, CLI, and dashboard expose agent runs, while a Postgres event log lets workers resume them after crashes.

item.title: Why Hardware Specialization Is Back (11 minute read)
item.description: Slower transistor scaling, memory bottlenecks, and power limits are renewing the case for specialized AI inference hardware. Matching different inference phases to different accelerators can improve performance per watt while adding deployment and software complexity and leaving room for GPUs to absorb successful ideas.

item.title: Evaluating Agents on Highly Subjective Tasks (20 minute read)
item.description: Reliable evaluation of open-ended agent tasks combines calibrated human judgments, automated judges or rubrics, and production monitoring. Power analysis, confidence intervals, and repeated runs help distinguish improvements from noise, while realistic, diverse tasks, and production feedback keep benchmarks useful.

item.title: Inside OpenAI's Jalapeño AI Chip (18 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's Jalapeño inference chip links 64 dedicated cores to individual HBM memory banks to reduce data movement and improve utilization. This interview explains the tradeoff in memory-management complexity, the choice to keep prefill and decode on fungible hardware, and how AI-assisted optimization accelerated chip design and kernel development.

item.description: Railway reports possible unauthorized access to customer environment variables, including some decrypted contents, and recommends rotating stored secrets and private registry credentials while reviewing service logs.

item.description: Google's Rust style guide covers code organization, formatting, ownership, API design, traits, errors, and concurrency.

item.description: Narrating your reasoning aloud can aid problem-solving by exposing assumptions, organizing dependencies, making rules explicit, and clarifying choices for backtracking.

item.description: OpenAI frontier models and Codex workflows are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden.

item.title: Try the Postgres that took Clera from 100% CPU to 10–20%, with $300 in free credits (Sponsor)
item.description: Clera is an AI talent agent. Its Postgres database was stuck at 100% CPU for six straight days. Primary-key lookups took three seconds, and writes failed under load.So they tested Supabase, Neon, PlanetScale and ClickHouse Managed Postgres on their own production data. ClickHouse won. They then migrated 500+ tables overnight, and CPU now typically runs at 10–20%.Read how other teams are succeeding with ClickHouse Managed Postgres.

item.title: Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform (10 minute read)
item.description: Ramp consolidated its agentic products onto an in-house, model-agnostic harness built on Postgres, Temporal, and S3. Session state lives independently of disposable sandboxes, while asynchronous steering, subagents, and shared tracing support everything from support chat to long-running knowledge work. The first version took six weeks to build, with experienced engineers steering and reviewing agent-generated code.

item.title: On Alignment That Looks Wrong (7 minute read)
item.description: Flexbox can center an SVG perfectly while the drawing inside still looks misplaced. Inspecting the viewport, correcting uneven viewBox space, and adjusting visual weight at the asset or component level produces better results than scattering pixel nudges across consumers. Play buttons, circle sizing, and hanging punctuation show why mathematical alignment and optical balance differ.

item.title: How to Build a Decision Model Like Jev (17 minute read)
item.description: Decision models return probabilities over known outcomes in a single forward pass, avoiding the text generation and JSON parsing overhead of chat completions. This walkthrough starts with Hugging Face's /v1/systemone endpoint, then covers reserved option tokens, calibration, soft training targets, and tree batching for multiple questions over shared context.

item.title: The Future of CSS: My Top 10 Picks for Interop 2027 (17 minute read)
item.description: Ten proposed Interop priorities include CSS functions, shaped borders, anchored container queries, visual reading order, and transitions to auto dimensions. Interactive examples show what each feature enables and where progressive enhancement can make it useful today. The case for staying current is practical: developers need enough CSS knowledge to guide coding agents beyond older patterns in their training data.

item.title: Gemini 4: Argon, Early Access Review (9 minute read)
item.description: Gemini 4 Argon handled an Android game, a UI redesign, and a distributed backend review well, with strong architectural planning and rapid changes across multiple files. Passing tests still hid cluttered layouts, accessibility regressions, and concurrency bugs, making browser checks, runtime logs, and adversarial self-review essential to getting reliable results.

item.title: Don't give your agent a token. Give it a proxy. (Sponsor)
item.description: What happens when you give your agent an access token and it gets hijacked? Relay (early access) keeps the credential at WorkOS and injects it only on requests to allowlisted hosts. A hijacked agent can still make bad calls, but it can't walk away with the token, and the session is a live process you can kill. Read the blog

item.title: TorchTPU (GitHub Repo)
item.description: TorchTPU provides a PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, with custom ATen kernels, an XLA compilation cache, and torch.compile integration. The repository includes distributed training support, debugging utilities, and examples for models including Llama, Qwen, and ResNet.

item.title: Introducing tsrs: A Port of TypeScript to Rust (6 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare and VoidZero, in collaboration with the TypeScript team, are developing tsrs as a faithful Rust port of TypeScript within the Oxc toolchain. Early matched-configuration benchmarks report up to 8x faster checking and about 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0. An experimental npm release is available, though compatibility differences remain before a stable release.

item.title: Voxtral 3 (8 minute read)
item.description: Mistral's Voxtral 3 combines transcription, expressive speech generation, and a voice agent SDK for streaming conversations with tool calls. Transcription supports more than 50 languages, while speech synthesis covers more than 35 languages and 50 dialects. The models are available through an EU-hosted API or self-deployment.

item.title: Do web components have a future if nobody is writing them? (11 minute read)
item.description: Agentic coding challenges the case for web components as a way to make scarce, handwritten code reusable. Google's Modern Web Guidance offers little encouragement for new custom elements, and the argument extends to JavaScript frameworks as code generation becomes cheaper. Sandboxing and reuse remain possible defenses, but each has limitations.

item.title: How Kiro Fixes Itself, and How We Keep the Fixes Honest (12 minute read)
item.description: Kiro mines its own execution traces to find wasted effort and propose prompt or tool changes, while deterministic gates test improvements against fresh controls and a permanent regression suite. Seven fixes merged in the first week, and a compaction change raised internal retention scores from 0.82 to 0.92. The reported gains come from internal experiments, and every accepted change still requires human code review.

item.title: From Use Case to GraphQL Operation: A Layered Approach for Agents (9 minute read)
item.description: A layered GraphQL approach lets agents start with local persisted operations, search an operation index, and reach for schema-driven query building or schema evolution only when needed. Persisting useful operations back into the index reduces repeated work, while fit evaluation determines when an existing query is sufficient and when the agent needs a more dynamic approach.

item.description: Rombo's open-source Tailwind CSS animation library provides configurable motion presets and a visual editor for creating animations and copying their utility classes.

item.description: eze turns an HTML folder into a self-hosted company website with shared sign-in, a database, live updates, file uploads, and AI access.

item.description: Data from 27 companies shows widely varying AI spending and PR output, with higher spend often failing to translate into faster shipping.

item.title: When Retries Make Things Worse: Protecting Your System From Overload (16 minute read)
item.description: Retries can turn a slow dependency into a wider outage by multiplying attempts and exhausting connections or workers. A PHP example combines one retry owner, an operation deadline, admission limits, shared retry budgets, and jitter, then outlines a load test that measures both overload and recovery.

item.title: The generic circular dependency problem (15 minute read)
item.description: Generic services become coupled to their consumers when shared types or domain logic pull application knowledge back into analytics, email, or authorization modules. Domain wrappers, locally owned handlers, smaller contracts, and plugin registration can break those cycles, while extracting a shared type package may only hide the conceptual coupling.

item.title: Making a website AI friendly: what the bots actually fetched from mine (17 minute read)
item.description: An analysis of 18 days of traffic to one personal site found that verified crawlers mostly fetched ordinary pages, robots.txt, and the sitemap. Markdown copies attracted verified crawlers within a day, while llms.txt saw no verified training or search crawler requests, suggesting that basic HTML and measured traffic matter more than adding every proposed discovery file.

item.title: Writing is no longer proof of work (6 minute read)
item.description: Organizations often use reports and templates as evidence that someone put in effort, followed a process, or understood a topic. LLMs weaken that signal by producing plausible documents without the underlying work, leaving companies to find better evidence and reserve careful writing for actual communication.

item.title: No more tech debt (4 minute read)
item.description: A completed design system migration shows how coding agents can make broad cleanup practical once reusable components, written guidance, and linters are in place. The team migrated through 45 pull requests across eight stacks, using vertical slices and before-and-after screenshots, then removed the old patterns so agents would stop copying them.

item.title: Developing Taste (3 minute read)
item.description: As working software becomes easier to produce, design, usability, and attention to detail become stronger differentiators. Taste develops through studying excellent work, explaining why specific choices succeed, and practicing with useful critique.

item.description: In a new survey, nearly 80% of developers said they give AI agents access to cloud environments, while 97% cited concerns about the security, cost, and quality implications of doing so. Read the report

item.description: Mac.apk implements the Android application environment directly on Apple Silicon Macs so apps run as native macOS processes with their own windows and GPU rendering. It is alpha software, with compatibility ranging from fully working apps to partial support or apps that do not launch.

item.title: Pele (Website)
item.description: Pele renders Mermaid diagrams as SVG with zero dependencies and CSS variable theming that can change colors without rendering again. The site reports a 230 kB gzipped bundle and support for every diagram type built into Mermaid 12.1.0, with layouts that adapt to small screens.

item.title: My experience running local LLMs (22 minute read)
item.description: Tests on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 system show why model size, memory bandwidth, context length, and serving engine all affect local agent performance. A quantized MoE model generated about 42 tokens per second for one request versus about 11 for a dense model, but the experiments measured generation speed rather than completed coding tasks.

item.title: Your coding agent loses its cache while it waits for you (19 minute read)
item.description: A survey of agent inference research distinguishes cache misses caused by memory pressure from those caused by human pauses. One public trace reported about 97% cache reuse after tool calls but 18% after gaps longer than an hour, highlighting a retention problem that autonomous benchmark loops often miss.

item.title: Agentic Monitoring (10 minute read)
item.description: Agents with access to code and telemetry can create targeted monitoring plans and investigate unusual signals around releases or configuration changes. An early prototype produced cleaner signals and used fewer tokens when an agent wrote monitoring specifications for a deterministic runner, with another agent investigating triggers and escalating to humans.

item.title: Humans approve intent, machines prove conformance (8 minute read)
item.description: Gittifacts routes agent-written changes to auto-merge, quick review, or full review based on test evidence and repository policy, after a human approves the plan. Missing signals can only increase scrutiny, and feature flags make merged changes reversible. Auto-merge still relies on the submitting agent's test environment for some evidence, while evidence generation took 13 to 17 minutes per change on the project's own repository.

item.title: HybridAgent Thinks in Latent Space and Acts in Text (6 minute read)
item.description: HybridAgent is a research approach for training AI agents to reason internally using numerical representations instead of writing out every intermediate thought, while still producing text to call tools such as Python or web search and deliver answers. In tests, a 14B Qwen3 model trained this way scored 52.4 on GAIA versus 43.7 for a matched text-only agent, with estimated decoding costs falling from $470 to $176 per million questions.

item.title: Exploring AWS Lambda Web Functions for building web applications (9 minute read)
item.description: AWS Lambda Web Functions run standard Node.js HTTP servers without adapters, with each execution environment handling concurrent requests and streaming responses. In a sample run of 300 streaming requests with up to 200 open at once, five environments consumed 4.75 seconds of CPU. Billing covers active CPU, memory, and requests, so waiting on a database or API uses little CPU but still incurs other charges.

item.title: Someone Behind the Software (3 minute read)
item.description: Good products reflect a shared point of view shaped by experience, customer conversations, and judgment. When teams use agents to add features independently, individually useful changes can weaken the product's coherence unless someone keeps shaping the whole.

item.title: What Requirements Don't You Have? (7 minute read)
item.description: Elegant systems often gain simplicity and scale by accepting limits on freshness, coordination, or flexibility. Coding agents tend to invent extra requirements, so explicitly stating which compromises are acceptable can prevent unnecessary locks, checks, and layers of abstraction.

item.title: Does Ruby on Rails Still Make Sense? (8 minute read)
item.description: Frameworks remain useful when agents write the code because they supply structure, shared maintenance, and familiar abstractions. Rewriting an application in a faster language can change behavior that users rely on, making targeted optimization and dependency updates a more practical starting point. Familiar code also makes it easier to review the decisions an agent makes.

In this webinar, we'll cover what context failure actually costs, in tokens, time and output quality. Save your spot.

item.title: DeepSeek Search & Fetch (Website)
item.description: DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs give agents and RAG applications live search results and web pages converted to Markdown. Both use standard DeepSeek API keys and cost $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests, with empty results, failures, and timeouts excluded from billing.

item.title: Sphinx (Website)
item.description: Sphinx pauses pushes to protected branches and quizzes developers on what agent-written code does, including failure scenarios. A separate reviewer reads the diff without seeing the development chat, explains incorrect answers, and asks a new scenario before allowing the push. It supports existing coding agents and configurable model endpoints, with a logged bypass for skipped checks.

item.title: Rakazo (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Rakazo is an open-source, self-hosted AI assistant for running persistent bots with their own memory, routines, and conversations. Bots can use browsers, terminals, files, and desktop interfaces, with your choice of model and local or hosted computer environments. The project is in beta and offers web, desktop, and mobile clients.

item.title: Claude Reveals ECDSA Curve Origins (9 minute read)
item.description: An internal Claude research model traced the seeds of five NIST prime curves to the lrand48 random-number generator initialized with Unix timestamps, explaining a decades-old provenance mystery. Anthropic says the findings strengthen confidence in the curves and do not reveal a cryptographic break. Some base-point origins, skipped candidates, and one binary-curve seed remain unexplained.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon vs. Claude Opus 5.5 (7 minute read)
item.description: In a comparison run once per model, Gemini 4 Argon matched Claude Opus 5.5 on finding and fixing 14 planted bugs at lower cost, but performed worse on billing and long-context dependency tasks. One incorrect API call caused most billing failures, and a manual one-line fix brought Argon to full marks. Its long-context answers still missed or invented dependencies, showing why the results need to be read beyond the headline scores.

item.title: Building a computer that can pause and resume in milliseconds: Inside the MicroVM architecture behind Managed Agents (20 minute read)
item.description: DigitalOcean's Firecracker platform separates agent sessions from their hosts using checkpointed disk, memory, and virtual-device state, with lazy loading to avoid downloading whole snapshots before resuming. Internal tests report under 200 milliseconds at p50 on the warm-template path, while external connections and API side effects remain outside the checkpoint.

item.title: Build the agent. Don't build its computer (20 minute read)
item.description: Agent teams should specify their execution environment, test recovery on real workloads, and start with managed infrastructure unless ownership offers a concrete advantage. The evaluation checklist covers persistent files, expired logins, interrupted external actions, access boundaries, and cost per accepted result.

item.title: How Meta Built Forum With AI-Native Engineering (8 minute read)
item.description: Meta built Forum with agents participating in planning, implementation, testing, and verification while engineers retained architectural judgment and final sign-off. The team improved results through simpler code, tools that inspect live app state, repeatable UI stress tests, and a separate build that excludes prototype code from production.

item.title: What I Self-Host (15 minute read)
item.description: A home server runs 28 services, including Jellyfin, Immich, Home Assistant, and Vaultwarden, on a mini PC with 16 GB of RAM. The setup favors simple native services and systemd-managed Podman containers, keeps services behind a VPN, and rejects tools whose operational complexity outweighs their value.

item.title: Code Is a Commodity Now (11 minute read)
item.description: Cheaper code generation could push software agencies away from selling development hours and toward domain expertise, product judgment, and accountability for outcomes. The essay argues that smaller generalist teams and changing hiring signals follow from this shift, while acknowledging mixed productivity evidence and the cost of verifying changes in mature codebases.

item.title: How to Measure the Human Cost of Agent Work (8 minute read)
item.description: Measure agent workflows by the human effort and agent spend required to reach an accepted result, including time spent briefing, supervising, reviewing, correcting, and verifying the work. Keep failed attempts and manual rescues in the totals so successful tasks do not hide the cost of unsuccessful ones. Track quality and later defects alongside time, and compare similar tasks under the same acceptance criteria before claiming productivity gains.

item.title: Vector search can't tell which memory is current (Sponsor)
item.description: Plain vector retrieval returns the old preference and the new one, and passing stale context to an LLM leads to hallucinations and conflicting actions. Graph-aware retrieval fixes this at the database layer with typed edges linking each memory to the one it replaced, and lifecycle flags marking what's active. The agent gets a clean current state, and the full history stays intact. Read the technical breakdown & companion notebook

item.title: Deploy with Void (7 minute read)
item.description: Void combines an open-source deployment platform, SDK, and CLI to bring full-stack development and Cloudflare deployment into a Vite workflow. It infers resource bindings and provisions infrastructure during deployment, while the shared platform lets administrators control team access, resource limits, and deployments.

item.title: Muse Spark Open (4 minute read)
item.description: Meta has released Muse Spark Open, a multimodal model with 816 billion total parameters, 42 billion active parameters, and a one-million-token context window. It supports coding and agentic workflows through hosted APIs or local inference, including on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios, with weights available under a license that includes limited commercial terms.

item.title: Introducing Devin Oncall (11 minute read)
item.description: Devin Oncall is generally available for investigating and remediating production issues, using company-specific skills and memory alongside a coding agent. Responders group related alerts and skip known issues, while an asynchronous review agent challenges unsupported diagnoses and premature conclusions.

item.title: What today's software owes to Bronze Age clocks (9 minute read)
item.description: Leaky buckets provide cheap admission control by calculating available capacity from a stored level and timestamp whenever new work arrives. The article connects this approach to API rate limits and PlanetScale's Postgres Traffic Control, which uses resource budgets to admit or block queries before execution and recommends testing budgets in warning mode first.

item.title: How Close Are We To Fully Autonomous Chip Design? (21 minute read)
item.description: Synopsys describes using orchestrated task agents to turn specifications into verified RTL, while full autonomy through physical implementation and chip sign-off remains a goal. Human engineers still define architectures and approve manufacturing, with advanced packaging and physical AI adding demands for coordinated multiphysics analysis.

item.title: How Codex Happened (38 minute read)
item.description: Codex emerged from parallel efforts in research automation and coding-product design, followed by a pivot after the initial cloud product struggled to find traction. The account traces the shift toward local workflows, a shared Rust agent core, and models trained for interactive work in messy codebases.

item.description: A shared TypeScript domain layer gives Next.js and Expo common types, validation schemas, and an API client while keeping platform-specific behavior inside each app.

item.title: Open weight takes 71.5% of tokens and 23% of spend (7 minute read)
item.description: Vercel's October AI Gateway index reports that open-weight models handled 71.5% of September tokens and 23% of estimated spend, while average price per token fell 47% from December.

item.title: How we made a 9 MB WebAssembly module feel faster without removing a single byte (11 minute read)
item.description: Earlier loading, preload hints, and shared initialization promises made a 9.2 MB Skia WebAssembly module render its first canvas roughly 17% to 18% faster in the reported A/B test without meaningfully shrinking the download.

item.title: Mo' turns, mo' problems (5 minute read)
item.description: Long agentic reinforcement-learning rollouts make harness state, tool-call serialization, branching trajectories, and numerical differences between inference and training harder to keep consistent.

item.title: The Most Common Questions About Agent Evals, Answered (8 minute read)
item.description: Agent evals score runs against desired behaviors, but exact-output tests often fail because agent outputs and paths vary. item.title: Lazy Loading Images and Media: How Far Ahead Browsers Fetch (6 minute read)
item.description: Browsers fetch lazy-loaded media at different distances, with Chrome adjusting its margin based on connection speed, Firefox using a fixed 600-pixel threshold, and Safari applying a viewport-based threshold to images. The article explains why the largest contentful paint image should load eagerly and why media dimensions should be reserved to prevent layout shifts. Its practical takeaway is to use native lazy loading selectively, based on how far ahead each browser fetches.

item.title: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers (7 minute read)
item.description: GitHub rebuilt its star-history API to return up to 30 weeks of daily counts in one request. Maintainers can track a project's momentum without exposing stargazer identities, which could be scraped for spam or phishing. To avoid simply shifting the cost to count queries, the endpoint filters stars by time before counting, reducing database work.

item.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era (6 minute read)
item.description: The article revisits the idea that UI should be a pure function of state and explains why it matters for agent-written interfaces. Passing roles, plans, billing status, and feature flags explicitly lets teams render and inspect each state combination before release.

item.title: Passkeys Are Not a Trap (4 minute read)
item.description: Synced consumer passkeys generally return no attestation, and WebAuthn attestation identifies an authenticator model rather than a user's operating system, browser, or firmware. The response argues that passkeys remain more phishing-resistant than TOTP and recommends continuing to use them.

item.description: AI agents and assistants now browse, buy, and fetch content for users, so “block all bots” policies end up blocking business. item.title: Rewinding the Exponential: How We Keep Hardware Usage Down (12 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare's data pipeline handles roughly two billion events per second while hardware capacity grows more slowly than traffic. item.title: Redesigning Source Control at Anthropic (14 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic replaced Git with Scion after daily merges grew from roughly 2,500 to more than 30,000. The centralized system uses server-side commits, sparse checkouts, and layered caches, reducing its source control infrastructure's CPU and memory footprint by 200 times and freeing 25% of CI CPU capacity.

item.title: A Year of Fast Apply: The Path to 10k Tokens per Second (13 minute read)
item.description: Relace explains how it built a small model that applies code edits at a reported 10,000 tokens per second using high-quality merge data, LoRA fine-tuning, FP8 quantization, and speculative decoding. Its training pipeline filtered 200,000 candidate examples down to about 145,000, using a judge calibrated against 500 manually reviewed merges. Relace Apply 3 supports a 256,000-token context and multiple diff formats, although improving frontier-model edit accuracy could eventually reduce the need for specialized apply models.

item.description: Programming for curiosity and enjoyment can restore motivation without requiring a business case or a finished product. This presentation suggests small experiments, toy implementations, language exploration, and documenting the process, with permission to switch projects or stop when they stop being fun.

item.description: More ambitious AI use can mean pursuing higher-level outcomes, applying expert methods to raw data, or combining ideas from multiple fields.
